Then $M$ decides $L$ in time $t$ if, for every input $x$, every computation path of $M$ on $x$ with at least $t(|x|)$ steps ends in a halted configuration, where $|x|$ is the length of $x$, and for every bitstring $x$, $x \in L$ if and only if some computation path of $M$…
nodes.title: Nondeterministic decision in bounded time

nodes.summary: A nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine $M$ over the boolean alphabet decides a set $L$ of bitstrings if, for every bitstring $x$, $x \in L$ if and only if some computation path of $M$ on $x$ ends in a halted configuration whose output is the one-element list $[\mathrm{true}]$.
nodes.title: Nondeterministic decision

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a one-way permutation family, so that each $\pi_n$ maps $n$-bit strings to $n$-bit strings. Then the family that sends an $n$-bit string $x$ to the bitstring $\pi_n(x)$ is a one-way function family.
nodes.title: One-way permutations are one-way functions

nodes.summary: An optimization problem consists of a function $v$ assigning a rational value $v(x, s)$ to every instance $x$ and every candidate solution $s$, both bitstrings; a feasibility predicate saying whether $s$ is a feasible solution for $x$; and a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients such that every feasible solution $s$ for $x$ has length at most $p(|x|)$. It is required that $v(x, s) \ge 0$ for all $x$ and…
nodes.title: Optimization problems

nodes.summary: A polynomial-time machine has polynomially bounded encoded output.
nodes.title: Polynomial-time machines have polynomially bounded output

nodes.summary: The parity decision problem accepts a bitstring exactly when an odd number of its entries are true.
nodes.title: The parity language

nodes.summary: For functions $r, q : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the class $\mathrm{PCP}(r, q)$ consists of the decision problems $L$ for which there are polynomial-time computable functions $Q$ and $D$ such that $Q(x, \rho)$ is a list of at most $q(|x|)$ natural numbers for all bitstrings $x$ and $\rho$, and such that for every bitstring $x$ the following holds. For a proof…
nodes.title: Probabilistically checkable proofs

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a family of maps $\pi_n$ from $n$-bit strings to $n$-bit strings, let $A$ be a function sending a natural number and two bitstrings to a bitstring, and let $n$ and $m$ be natural numbers. For a bitstring $w$, write $\mathrm{trunc}_n(w)$ for the $n$-bit string whose bit at each position $i < n$ is the entry of $w$ at position $i$, or false if $w$ has at most $i$ entries. The success probability of $A$…
nodes.title: Inversion success probability against a permutation family

nodes.summary: The class PH is the union, over all natural numbers $k$, of the classes $\Sigma_k^p$ of the polynomial hierarchy.
nodes.title: The polynomial hierarchy

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, the class $\Pi_k^p$ consists of the decision problems $L$ for which there are a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients and a polynomial-time computable function $R$, taking a bitstring and a list of bitstrings to a boolean, such that for every bitstring $x$, $L(x)$ is true if and only if
nodes.title: The universal levels of the polynomial hierarchy

nodes.summary: The class PP consists of the decision problems $L$ for which there are a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients and a polynomial-time computable function $R$ on pairs of bitstrings such that, for every bitstring $x$ and $r$ uniformly random among the bitstrings of length $p(|x|)$, the probability that $R(x, r)$ is true is greater than $1/2$ if $L(x)$ is true, and at most $1/2$ if $L(x)$ is false.
nodes.title: Probabilistic polynomial time with unbounded error

nodes.summary: The class P/poly consists of the decision problems $L$ for which there are a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients, bitstrings $a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots$ with $|a_n| \le p(n)$ for every $n$, and a polynomial-time computable function $R$ on pairs of bitstrings such that for every bitstring $x$, $L(x)$ is true if and only if $R(x, a_{|x|})$ is true.
nodes.title: Polynomial time with polynomial advice

nodes.summary: The class PSPACE of decision problems consists of the decision problems $L$ whose language $\{x : L(x) = \mathrm{true}\}$ lies in the multi-tape class PSPACE, that is, is decided by a multi-tape Turing machine that halts on every input and uses space $O(n^d)$ for some natural number $d$.
nodes.title: Polynomial space for decision problems

nodes.summary: Every optimization problem in the class PTAS belongs to the class APX.
nodes.title: PTAS is contained in APX

nodes.summary: PTAS is the set of optimization problems $P$ that are NPO problems (feasibility is decidable in polynomial time and the objective value is given by a polynomial-time computable rational encoding) and that have a polynomial-time approximation scheme: for every natural number $k \ge 1$ there is a polynomial-time algorithm $A$ such that, for every instance $x$ and every feasible solution $s$ of $x$, the output of $A$…
nodes.title: The class PTAS

nodes.summary: For a Boolean oracle $O$ on bitstrings, the class $\mathsf{P}^O$ consists of the decision problems $L$ for which there are polynomials $p$ and $q$ and polynomial-time functions $\mathrm{next}$ and $\mathrm{final}$ such that, for every bitstring $x$, $L(x)$ is true exactly when the following oracle machine outputs true on $x$. Starting from the empty history $h$, it runs $p(|x|)$ rounds; in each round it computes…
nodes.title: Polynomial time with an oracle

nodes.summary: The class $\mathsf{P}^{\#\mathsf{P}}$ consists of the decision problems $L$ for which there are a function $f$ in $\#\mathsf{P}$, polynomials $p$ and $q$, and polynomial-time functions $\mathrm{next}$ and $\mathrm{final}$ such that, for every bitstring $x$, $L(x)$ is true exactly when the following oracle machine outputs true on $x$. Starting from the empty history $h$, it runs $p(|x|)$ rounds; in each round it…
nodes.title: Polynomial time with a #P oracle

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $i$, this is the digit of $i$ at position $k$ in binary, counting from the least significant digit at position $0$, that is, $\lfloor i / 2^k \rfloor \bmod 2$, taken as an element of $\{0, 1\}$.
nodes.title: Binary digit of a natural number

nodes.summary: A pair $(a, b)$ of bits $a, b \in \{0, 1\}$ has index $2a + b$, its position in the enumeration $(0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1)$ of the four pairs.
nodes.title: Index of a pair of bits

nodes.summary: A list $b_0, b_1, \ldots, b_{n-1}$ of booleans, read as bits with true as $1$ and false as $0$, denotes the natural number $\sum_{i < n} b_i 2^i$; the first entry is the least significant bit.
nodes.title: Number with a given binary expansion

nodes.summary: A 2-local gate acting on qubits $i$ and $j$ with entry list $e$ is well-formed on $N$ qubits when $i < j < N$ and the $4 \times 4$ complex matrix $U$ encoded by $e$ is unitary, that is, $U^* U = I$.
nodes.title: Well-formed quantum gate

nodes.summary: A 2-local quantum gate is encoded as a triple $(i, j, e)$ of natural numbers $i$ and $j$, the qubits it acts on, and a list $e$ of pairs of encoded rational numbers, the real and imaginary parts of the entries of its $4 \times 4$ matrix in row-major order.
nodes.title: Encoded 2-local quantum gate

nodes.summary: A rational number is encoded as a triple $(s, a, b)$ of a boolean $s$ and natural numbers $a$ and $b$, read as the sign, the numerator and the denominator.
nodes.title: Encoded rational number

nodes.summary: Canonical polynomial-time maps can also be run on unframed bit lists.
nodes.title: Polynomial-time maps run on unframed bit lists

nodes.summary: A decision problem $L$ is in $\mathsf{RP}$ when there are a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients and a polynomial-time computable Boolean function $R$ on pairs of bitstrings such that for every bitstring $x$: if $L(x)$ is true, then $R(x, r)$ is true for at least half of the $2^{p(|x|)}$ bitstrings $r$ of length $p(|x|)$; and if $L(x)$ is false, then $R(x, r)$ is false for every bitstring $r$ of length…
nodes.title: The class RP

nodes.summary: Pulling SAT back along a polynomial map preserves NP membership. SAT verifier soundness holds even for certificates above its length bound.
nodes.title: Preimage of SAT under a polynomial-time map is in NP

nodes.summary: A serial circuit is a list of pairs $(k, \ell)$, where $k$ is a natural number (the gate kind) and $\ell$ is a list of natural numbers (the gate's references).
nodes.title: Serial circuits

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a list of Boolean values of earlier gates, let $a$ assign a Boolean to each of the $n$ inputs $0, \dots, n - 1$, and let $(k, \ell)$ be a serialized gate. Write $v_c$ for entry $c$ of $v$, read as false when $c$ is out of range. The value of the gate is: $a(i)$ if $(k, \ell) = (0, [i])$ with $i < n$, and false if $(k, \ell) = (0, [i])$ with $i \ge n$; true exactly when $b = 1$ if $(k, \ell) = (1, [b])$;…
nodes.title: Evaluating a serialized gate

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $N$, $s$, $i$, $j$ and a pair $b = (b_1, b_2)$ of bits, this is the index in $\{0, \dots, 2^N - 1\}$ given by $(s - s_i 2^i - s_j 2^j + b_1 2^i + b_2 2^j) \bmod 2^N$, where $s_k$ is bit $k$ of $s$ and each subtraction of natural numbers is truncated at $0$. When $i \ne j$ this is $s$ with bit $i$ set to $b_1$ and bit $j$ set to $b_2$, reduced modulo $2^N$.
nodes.title: Setting two bits of an index

nodes.summary: A function $f$ from bitstrings to natural numbers is in $\#P$ when there are a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients and a polynomial-time computable Boolean function $R$ on pairs of bitstrings such that for every bitstring $x$, $f(x)$ is the number of bitstrings $w$ of length exactly $p(|x|)$ for which $R(x, w)$ is true.
nodes.title: The counting class $\#P$

nodes.summary: A function $f$ from bitstrings to natural numbers is $\#P$-complete when $f$ is in $\#P$ and every function $g$ in $\#P$ is computed from $f$ by a polynomial-time oracle machine. That is, there are polynomials $p$ and $q$ with natural-number coefficients and polynomial-time computable functions choosing the next query and the final natural-number answer from the input and the history of queries and oracle answers,…
nodes.title: $\#P$-complete functions

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, a decision problem $L$ is in $\Sigma_k^p$ when there are a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients and a polynomial-time computable Boolean function $R$ of a bitstring and a list of bitstrings such that for every bitstring $x$, $L(x)$ is true if and only if $Q_1 w_1\, Q_2 w_2 \cdots Q_k w_k$ with $R(x, [w_1, \dots, w_k])$ true, where $Q_i$ is $\exists$ for odd $i$ and $\forall$ for…
nodes.title: The class $\Sigma_k^p$

nodes.summary: For a vector $\psi \in \mathbb{C}^{2^m}$, indexed by $\{0, \dots, 2^m - 1\}$, its squared norm is the real number $\sum_{s} \overline{\psi_s}\, \psi_s = \sum_{s} |\psi_s|^2$.
nodes.title: Squared norm of a state vector

nodes.summary: For vectors $\varphi \in \mathbb{C}^{2^a}$ and $\psi \in \mathbb{C}^{2^b}$, indexed by $\{0, \dots, 2^a - 1\}$ and $\{0, \dots, 2^b - 1\}$, their tensor product is the vector in $\mathbb{C}^{2^{a+b}}$ whose entry at $s$ is $\varphi_{s \bmod 2^a}\, \psi_{\lfloor s / 2^a \rfloor}$. Thus $\varphi$ occupies the low-order $a$ bits of the index and $\psi$ the high-order $b$ bits.
nodes.title: Tensor product of state vectors

nodes.summary: A pair $(e_1, e_2)$ of rational encodings encodes the complex number $q_1 + q_2 i$, where $q_1$ and $q_2$ are the rational numbers encoded by $e_1$ and $e_2$.
nodes.title: Complex number of a pair of rational encodings

nodes.summary: A triple $(s, p, q)$, with $s$ a boolean and $p, q$ natural numbers, encodes the rational number $-p/q$ when $s$ is true and $p/q$ when $s$ is false; when $q = 0$ the value is $0$, since division by zero gives $0$.
nodes.title: Rational number of an encoding

nodes.summary: A family $(C_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of flat Boolean circuits, $C_n$ having $n$ inputs, is log-space uniform when there is a log-space computable function $D$ on bitstrings such that, for every $n$, decoding $D(1^n)$ (where $1^n$ is the string of $n$ ones) as a list of (gate kind, references) pairs succeeds and returns the serial encoding of $C_n$, that is, the list of the serial encodings of its gates in order.…
nodes.title: Log-space uniform circuit families

nodes.summary: A flat Boolean circuit on $n$ inputs, given as a list of gates $(g_0, \dots, g_{m-1})$, is well-formed when every gate references only strictly earlier gates: for every $j < m$, every gate index $a$ among the inputs of $g_j$ satisfies $a < j$.
nodes.title: Well-formed flat circuits

nodes.summary: The all-zero state on $a$ qubits is the vector in $\mathbb{C}^{2^a}$, indexed by $s \in \{0, \dots, 2^a - 1\}$, whose entry at $s = 0$ is $1$ and whose other entries are $0$; that is, the computational basis state $|0 \cdots 0\rangle$.
nodes.title: All-zero state

nodes.summary: The class $\mathsf{ZPP}$ equals $\mathsf{RP} \cap \mathsf{coRP}$; here this holds by definition.
nodes.title: ZPP is the intersection of RP and coRP

nodes.summary: Every decision problem in $\mathsf{ZPP}$ lies in $\mathsf{coRP}$, that is, $\mathsf{ZPP} \subseteq \mathsf{coRP}$.
nodes.title: ZPP is contained in coRP

nodes.summary: Every decision problem in $\mathsf{ZPP}$ lies in $\mathsf{RP}$, that is, $\mathsf{ZPP} \subseteq \mathsf{RP}$.
nodes.title: ZPP is contained in RP

nodes.summary: The class $\mathsf{ZPP}$ (zero-error probabilistic polynomial time) is defined as the set of decision problems that lie in both $\mathsf{RP}$ and $\mathsf{coRP}$, that is, $\mathsf{ZPP} = \mathsf{RP} \cap \mathsf{coRP}$.
nodes.title: ZPP

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
